title: $q$-deformation as a contact metric change (Miranda picture)
html:
Remark. q-deformation as a contact metric change (Miranda picture)

The Cardona–Miranda–Peralta-Salas–Presas [cardona2021] procedure bridges steady Euler flow and contact-Reeb flow through a conformal change of metric. Given a divergence-free, non-vanishing Euler field X on (M^3, g), rescaling X \mapsto X / |X|_g^2 and factoring the metric maps X to the Reeb vector field of a contact form on (M^3, \tilde g). The dynamical universality derives from the contact structure, not the initial metric.

The QOU executes exactly this operation via the substrate parameter q. The q-Navier–Stokes equation replaces the classical Riemannian inner product with the q-deformed Frobenius pairing (Frobenius–Hopf substrate). This constitutes a one-parameter family of metric adjustments, smoothly modulating between:

  • the full Levi-Civita connection (the "Euler-side" geometry representing Riemannian fluid flow), and
  • its Reeb projection along \xi_q (the "contact-side" geometry isolating pure Reeb flow).

The parameter q acts as the dial. Three regimes govern the behaviour:

Parameter limit Geometric picture Dynamical content
q \to 1^+ Full Riemannian metric; \varTheta_q degenerates Classical Navier–Stokes; Reeb projection vanishes
q > 1 generic Strict contact metric on \mathcal{S} q-NS globally regular (thm:q-ns-wellposedness); Reeb flow Turing-complete (rem:reeb-contact-universal-computer)
q \to \infty Pure Reeb (horizontal components vanish) Hamiltonian first-return; bare tape-reading dynamics

A geometric reading of the q-NS obstruction. The NS obstruction class gauges how the classical q = 1 contact form collapses at a vortex-collision locus. Through Miranda's framework, increasing q past 1 rescales the Riemannian metric to buoy the contact form against degeneracy. The Levi form condition number isolates this contact degeneracy; it is the exact metric property that the q-deformation corrects. The quantum pressure term acts as an isotropic buffer preventing the Levi eigenvalues from crossing zero.

Location in the proof strategy. The q-NS research programme incorporates two implications:

  1. Global well-posedness for q > 1 (thm:q-ns-wellposedness) versus breakdown at q = 1 is a feature of the smooth-vs-degenerate contact dichotomy, not an independent quantum effect.
  2. The Levi degeneracy conjecture isolates whether a given vortex collision targets the metric-Riemannian (regular) limit, where the contact form dies and the flow flattens, or the contact (blowup) limit, where the metric isolates non-degenerate dynamics. The Biot–Savart and hyperbolic overlap remarks frame these regimes explicitly as ODEs.

In the Cardona–Miranda grammar: the parameter q selects the contact metric, and that choice determines whether the Reeb dynamics persists or triggers a contact-degenerate singularity.
